hints: Apply the tangent addition formula to $\tan(\alpha+\beta)=2$ while keeping the restrictions $0^\circ<\alpha,\beta<180^\circ$ in view.
Substitute $\tan\alpha=3\tan\beta$ to obtain a quadratic in one tangent value.
Solve the quadratic, then find all angles in the stated interval corresponding to each positive or negative tangent value.
Pair the angles so that both $\tan\alpha=3\tan\beta$ and the original sum condition hold; work consistently in degrees.
walkthrough:
State the compound angle addition formula for tangent:
$$\tan(\alpha + \beta) = \dfrac{\tan\alpha + \tan\beta}{1 - \tan\alpha\tan\beta}$$

Substitute the given relation $\tan\alpha = 3\tan\beta$ into the equation:
$$3\tan\beta + \tan\beta = 2 - 2(3\tan\beta)\tan\beta$$
$$4\tan\beta = 2 - 6\tan^2\beta$$

Rearrange into a standard quadratic equation in $\tan\beta$:
$$6\tan^2\beta + 4\tan\beta - 2 = 0$$
Divide through by $2$ to simplify:
$$3\tan^2\beta + 2\tan\beta - 1 = 0$$

Factorise the three-term quadratic equation:
Find two numbers with product $3 \times (-1) = -3$ and sum $2$, which are $3$ and $-1$:
$$3\tan^2\beta + 3\tan\beta - \tan\beta - 1 = 0$$
$$3\tan\beta(\tan\beta + 1) - 1(\tan\beta + 1) = 0$$
$$(3\tan\beta - 1)(\tan\beta + 1) = 0$$
This gives two possible values for $\tan\beta$:
$$\tan\beta = \dfrac{1}{3} \quad \text{or} \quad \tan\beta = -1$$

Case 1: $\tan\beta = \dfrac{1}{3}$
Since $\tan\beta > 0$ and $0^\circ < \beta < 180^\circ$, $\beta$ lies in the first quadrant:
$$\beta = \arctan\left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right) \approx 18.4349^\circ \approx 18.4^\circ$$
Calculate $\tan\alpha = 3\tan\beta = 3\left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right) = 1$:
$$\alpha = \arctan(1) = 45^\circ$$
Check the sum: $\alpha + \beta = 45^\circ + 18.4349^\circ = 63.4349^\circ$, and $\tan(63.4349^\circ) = 2$.
This gives the first solution pair: $\alpha = 45^\circ$ and $\beta = 18.4^\circ$.

Case 2: $\tan\beta = -1$
Since $\tan\beta < 0$ and $0^\circ < \beta < 180^\circ$, $\beta$ lies in the second quadrant:
$$\beta = 180^\circ - \arctan(1) = 180^\circ - 45^\circ = 135^\circ$$
Calculate $\tan\alpha = 3\tan\beta = 3(-1) = -3$:
Since $\tan\alpha < 0$ and $0^\circ < \alpha < 180^\circ$, $\alpha$ lies in the second quadrant:
$$\alpha = 180^\circ - \arctan(3)$$
With $\arctan(3) \approx 71.5651^\circ$:
$$\alpha = 180^\circ - 71.5651^\circ = 108.4349^\circ \approx 108.4^\circ$$
Check the sum: $\alpha + \beta = 108.4349^\circ + 135^\circ = 243.4349^\circ$, and $\tan(243.4349^\circ) = \tan(243.4349^\circ - 180^\circ) = \tan(63.4349^\circ) = 2$.
This gives the second solution pair: $\alpha = 108.4^\circ$ and $\beta = 135^\circ$.

State both possible pairs of angles $(\alpha, \beta)$:
$$(\alpha, \beta) = (45^\circ, 18.4^\circ) \quad \text{or} \quad (108.4^\circ, 135^\circ)$$

ai_rubric.Solving Trigonometric Equations: Applies the $\tan(A+B)$ formula and derives an equation in $\tan\alpha$ and $\tan\beta$; Derives $3\tan^2\beta+2\tan\beta-1=0$ or $\tan^2\alpha+2\tan\alpha-3=0$, or equivalent; Concludes with $(\alpha,\beta)=(45^\circ,18.4^\circ)$ or $(108.4^\circ,135^\circ)$.
